objective: Make every documented repository path honest: resolve or remove the references that name files which are not committed, and add a committed check that fails a build when a backticked repository path in docs/** or a module README does not exist, wired into make docs so foundation-checks catches a new dangling reference without a new workflow.
decision_supported: Does a reference in committed documentation name a path a reader who clones the repository can actually open, and does a build fail when one does not?
acceptance: Every reference the issue lists either resolves to a committed file, is replaced by the content it pointed at, or is removed with a sentence explaining what a reader loses.

ADR-0004 no longer cites robot/control/PLAN.md; it quotes the two Phase 1 gates it is measured against (verify the vendor package first, and reach 95% reachability) so the decision stands on committed text, and its decision text is otherwise unchanged.
robot/control/README.md states that the construction plan is kept local instead of presenting PLAN.md as a path a reader can open.
hardware/arm_drivers/README.md no longer points at a cross-compilation note that was never written, and makes no cross-compilation claim.
tasks/pick_place/README.md names services/world_model/workbench_world_model/verifier.py::verify_object_in_tray and says why verification lives in the world model.

A committed check, tools/scripts/check_doc_references.py, fails a build when a backticked repository path in a Markdown file under docs/** or in a module README does not exist, with an allowlist for the deliberately-local robot/control/PLAN.md named explicitly.
The check is wired into make docs, so foundation-checks catches a new dangling reference without a new workflow.

The check resolves a reference from the repository root, the page's directory, docs/, or as the tail of a real path; bare filenames and runs/ artifacts are out of scope, which is stated in the module.
Exit codes are 0 PASS, 1 FAIL and 2 INCOMPLETE, and an unreadable root is INCOMPLETE rather than PASS.
A deliberately broken reference fails the check with exit code 1 and fails make docs before mkdocs runs.
No ADR is rewritten beyond the citation and no schema, contract model, workflow or ruleset changes.

stop_conditions: Resolving a reference would require publishing a document that contains private design content; the correct outcome there is to delete the reference and say so, not to publish the document.
The check would have to be weakened to a bare-filename scan that fails pages documenting generated reports; that is the wrong fix and the boundary stays at path-bearing references.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to robot/control/** outside its README or to any firmware path.
Resolving a reference would require changing an ADR's decision text rather than its citation.
The change would need a new workflow to run the check; it must ride make docs instead.
data_classification: Repository-local Markdown and Python. No credentials, private data or unreviewed assets are read, written or logged.
model_policy: Deterministic Python and a local pytest run; no model inference and no network access added by this change.
risks_and_fallbacks: The check could reject a legitimate page that cites a path in a form it does not resolve. The risk is bounded because it reads only code spans carrying a path separator and a known extension, and resolves four ways including a path-tail match; a page that trips it is either wrong or one allowlist entry away from being right, and the entry has to be justified in the module.

The allowlist for robot/control/PLAN.md is a permanent exclusion that could hide a future dangling reference. It is a named constant with its reason recorded rather than a silent skip, so publishing the plan is what makes the citation start being checked.

Rollback is a revert of this commit: delete the check, restore the six pages and drop the Makefile line. No code path reads these documents, so nothing depends on the change; the only loss is the failure detection.
